body:
## Problem

FreeBSD and OpenBSD are Tier 2 supported platforms (`:help
supported-platforms`) but have had no CI coverage since #39321 dropped the
Cirrus config. From the review there:

> I thought about changing these to `is_os(bsd)`, but I think instead we can
> wait until we have BSD CI, and then reintroduce as necessary.

## Solution

Add a `bsd` workflow with one FreeBSD and one OpenBSD build job, using
[vmactions](https://github.com/vmactions), which boots the guest under
QEMU/KVM on a regular `ubuntu-latest` runner.

vmactions was evaluated in #19616 back in 2022 and set aside for two
reasons. Neither still applies:

| 2022 objection | today |
|---|---|
| "It requires macos as the runner, which github is stingy with" | runs on `ubuntu-latest`; no macOS minutes consumed |
| "The vms have the performance of a potato" | full deps + nvim build in 3m32s (FreeBSD) / 4m37s (OpenBSD) |

## Verification

https://github.com/neilpang/neovim/actions/runs/30680480936

```
FreeBSD  [682/688] Linking C executable bin/nvim
         NVIM v0.13.0-dev-bca238e, LuaJIT 2.1.1785005726
OpenBSD  [682/687] Linking C executable bin/nvim
         NVIM v0.13.0-dev-bca238e, LuaJIT 2.1.1785005726
```

The other checks on that PR (build, test, codeql, zizmor, wasm) all passed
as well, so the change does not disturb the existing pipeline.

## Points for you to decide

1. **Build only, no tests** -- matching the suggestion in #19616 ("Let's
   only build, then. Don't run the tests."). The old Cirrus job also ran
   functionaltest/unittest/oldtest; those can be added if you want the
   coverage, at the cost of a longer job.
2. **Cache usage** is ~4.15 GB of the 10 GB quota (VM images, including
   `cache-after-prepare`). Dropping `cache-after-prepare` saves ~2.6 GB but
   re-runs the package install on every job.
3. **The release is not pinned**, so the job follows the action's current
   default (FreeBSD 15.1 / OpenBSD 7.9). Cirrus needed a version-bump PR
   every few months; this avoids that. Pinning is one line if you prefer it.
4. `support.txt` still lists both as Tier 2 with an empty "Tested versions"
   column -- happy to fill that in, or leave the tier question to you.

comment_data.body:
`vmactions/freebsd-vm@v1` is a third-party action pinned only to a moving major tag. This repo otherwise pins third-party actions to an immutable commit SHA (e.g. `.github/workflows/test.yml` uses `mlugg/setup-zig@<sha>`, `.github/workflows/backport.yml` uses `korthout/backport-action@<sha>`), and it also helps keep the `zizmor` unpinned-uses check happy.

This issue also appears on line 54 of the same file.

comment_regular_data.body: Never request reviews from copilot on PRs to this repo. Do it on your fork.

Yes -- I tried it, and it works. Here is what I measured, in case it helps
decide how to proceed.

I ran `functionaltest-parallel` on both platforms on top of this workflow.
Both need the tests to run as a non-root user, and each needs a different
piece of setup to get there:

- **FreeBSD**: `su -m` keeps `HOME=/root`, so any test writing under `$HOME`
  fails with EPERM. Setting `HOME` explicitly fixes it -- this is what
  `sudo -u` was doing for us on Cirrus.
- **OpenBSD**: the default login class caps `maxproc`/`openfiles` too low for
  the parallel runner, and the test client dies with `EAGAIN: resource
  temporarily unavailable`. Creating the test user in the `staff` class and
  using a login shell fixes it.

With that in place the suite runs to completion, and total wall time stays
close to the build-only job -- FreeBSD ~7.5 min, OpenBSD ~11.5 min, build
included. Failures are down to 8 per platform:

Run (deliberately left red -- those 8 genuinely fail):
https://github.com/neilpang/neovim/actions/runs/30706809855

- FreeBSD job: https://github.com/neilpang/neovim/actions/runs/30706809855/job/91387234338
- OpenBSD job: https://github.com/neilpang/neovim/actions/runs/30706809855/job/91387234358

That run is this PR's workflow plus the two environment fixes above; the
workflow proposed here is unchanged and green.

**FreeBSD**

```
lua/system_spec.lua @ 36           vim.system (sync) uses real pipes for stdin/stdout #35984
lua/system_spec.lua @ 36           vim.system (async) uses real pipes for stdin/stdout #35984
plugin/pack_spec.lua @ 605         vim.pack add() uses lockfile during install
plugin/zip_spec.lua @ 342          nvim.zip backend arguments treats archive glob characters literally
plugin/zip_spec.lua @ 459          nvim.zip extract extracts suspicious entries without escaping the cwd
terminal/ex_terminal_spec.lua @ 64 :terminal reads output buffer on terminal reporting #4151
vimscript/system_spec.lua @ 108    system() sets v:shell_error        (expected 127, got 126)
vimscript/system_spec.lua @ 415    systemlist() sets v:shell_error    (expected 127, got 126)
```

**OpenBSD**

```
lua/net_spec.lua @ 167             vim.net.request dispatches remote zip URLs to zip.lua
lua/system_spec.lua @ 36           vim.system (sync) uses real pipes for stdin/stdout #35984
lua/system_spec.lua @ 36           vim.system (async) uses real pipes for stdin/stdout #35984
plugin/pack_spec.lua @ 605         vim.pack add() uses lockfile during install
terminal/buffer_spec.lua @ 568     :terminal buffer handles suspended PTY resumed by an external signal
terminal/tui_spec.lua @ 2721       TUI in nvim_list_uis(), sets nvim_set_client_info()
terminal/tui_spec.lua @ 3407       TUI argv[0] can be overridden #23953
ui/diff_spec.lua @ 2475            diff mode inline highlighting
```

I left this out of the PR on purpose. Some of these are clearly platform
semantics that just want a skip -- the `v:shell_error` pair is 127 vs 126
(command-not-found vs found-but-not-executable), and OpenBSD does not permit
rewriting `argv[0]` at all. But others look like they could be real bugs
rather than quirks: `vim.system` real-pipes and the `vim.pack` lockfile test
fail *identically on both BSDs*, which is more suggestive of a portability bug
than of two unrelated platform differences. Blanket-skipping those would hide
exactly what this CI exists to catch, and telling them apart is a bigger job
than the workflow itself.

So I would rather land the build coverage first and follow up with a second PR
that turns on functionaltest plus whatever `skip(is_os('bsd'))` calls survive
triage. Happy to fold it in here instead if you would prefer it in one go.
